newsitem.title: UK: Hungary share market poised to rise in 1997-HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Hungary share market poised to rise in 1997-HSBC.

text.p: The Hungarian equity market, one the best performers in dollar terms globally this year, looks set to continue to rise next year, outperforming other markets in the region, HSBC James Capel said in a new report.
"The Hungarian equity market is poised for another strong performance in 1997," HSBC said in the November issue its Emerging Europe Investment Strategy.
"With few potential problems on the horizon Hungary looks set to outperform the other markets in the region," strategist Nigel Rendell said.

The Budapest Stock Exchange has been on an upward path most of this year, with the BUX index setting several new all time highs and peaking above 3,700 points from last year's close of 1,528.92 points.
HSBC points to two factors as main driving force behind the market's expected rise.
"The main supports will come from declining interest rates and a pick up in the domestic economy," Rendell's research said.
Hungarian interest rates have come down gradually this year and HSBC expects a fall by a further 100 basis points by end of this year and by another 200 basis points next year.

On the back of a recovery in the domestic economy HSBC expects to see a real GDP growth of up to three percent in 1997 as against a forecast of 0.8 percent this year, and predicted an earnings per share growth of 25 percent in 1997, up from an estimated 15 percent in 1996. HSBC said that while the budget and current account deficits are heading the right direction, the ongoing austerity drive is having a depressing impact on the domestic economy.

"Real wages are likely to fall by five percent this year and there may be some temptation for the authorities to boost public spending in the run up to the 1998 elections," the research said. -- Emese Bartha, London newsroom + 44 171 542-5887
